chapter: Carnegie Hall and the touring years
title: Herman the German, the Peacock Nightclub and years driving the South
summary: At Houston's Peacock he befriended emcee Herman the German, who then drove for him for ten or twelve years.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So we talkin' about whenever anybody would have a good night ...made some extra money...we'd all come out and have a good time the next day. I had a friend of mine called Herman the German. I met him down in Houston, Texas. I was workin' at a place called the Peacock Nightclub. Don Roby (?) run it, and, uh...we, uh, used to play there sometimes a month in the nightclub, and so I run into Herman the German

was in the checkroom when he was part-time manager there at the club. So he was married to a beautiful woman so he went and brought her over to the nightclub and put her in the checkroom. He shoulda never done that 'cause the cats had never seen a pretty woman like that before, and, uh, every cat that come into the joint would take his coat an' hat an' stuff. They'd hit on her.

So Herman was so busy. He was the emcee of the club an' runnin' the nightclub for th' Don Roby (?) he didn't have time to check up on her...his wife. So I used to tell him, I say, "You made a big mistake...puttin' your wife in the checkroom 'cause all them cats come in hit on her."
'N' he say, "Nahhhh, s'all right. Me 'n' her's tight."

So's went on 'bout like that. We's back an' forth in that nightclub, in an' out 'bout two...three years we'd go back an' forth. We'd go out an' aplay four weeks in a nightclub and play one-nighters. So Herman the German was still there.
So I was drivin' myself in my own car. I had a Buick. Eve'-body else had Cadillacs. So's the cats usedta tease me all the time, say, "Joe Turner, why'nt you get you a Cadillac?"
I told 'em, I say, "Well, I like my Buicks."

So, finally, we got together, an' Herman the German said he wanted to travel aroun' with me, so I tell 'im was okay. So I took Herman the German, an' he started drivin' for me. He was to...I didn't have to do no drivin'...only as when he got full of his good stuff an' partied too much, and I had to do the drivin'.

So, afterwards, we stay down there all summer, through Texas; Mississippi; Louisiana; all down through Arkansas; Nashville, Tennessee. We played every nightclub and every university there was. An' uh, I kept Herman with me ten...twelve years, back an' forth.
